1440, Gavin See › Files. noise.png (9,927,168 B, 1575 px RGBA) was redrawn on the client, so the action POST dropped to 2,245,055 characters, but the server still answered 500 and no file was made. The :3025 log reads '⨯ Error: Maximum array nesting exceeded. Large nested arrays can be dangerous.' The 12 MB body limit is not the cause. React's server-action reply decoder counts a string argument's length against its 1,000,000 arraySizeLimit whenever the argument list has more than one item, and uploadFile(leadId, parentId, name, image) passes the picture as a separate argument. A controlled run shows the threshold: photo-500k.jpg (data URL 321k chars) → 200, saved. photo-900k.jpg (830k) → 200, saved. photo-1m.jpg (a plain 1.05 MB, 1900×1300 JPEG, 1.40M chars) → 500, nothing saved, same log line. phone-4032.jpg (3 MB, 4032 px) → 200, because readFileAsDataUrl scaled it to 2000 px and re-encoded it to 305 KB. So the toast half is fixed (see the new-issue result), but ordinary photos around 750 KB and up still fail to upload.
results.remaining: Every JPEG, PNG or WebP under 2000 px whose data URL is over 1,000,000 characters (about 730 KB of file) fails with a 500, including the original 9.9 MB PNG. PICTURE_CAP = 8,000,000 in upload-picture.ts never takes effect. Fix: send the picture inside one object argument (uploadFile({ leadId, parentId, name, image })), because strings under an object are not counted, or send it as FormData or a Blob. Otherwise cap the data URL below 1,000,000 characters and redraw smaller. Check any other action that takes a big string as a separate argument too (e.g. saveQuoteText(quoteId, kind, html) with pasted images).

newIssues.title: Lead › Files refuses every picture over about 730 KB (a data URL over 1,000,000 characters) with a server 500 ('Maximum array nesting exceeded'), so ordinary site photos don't upload
newIssues.repro: Lead › Files › New File › upload a 1.05 MB, 1900×1300 JPEG (verify2/files/photo-1m.jpg), or the 9.9 MB noise.png.
newIssues.evidence: Action POST → 500, and no lead_files row is made. The :3025 log reads '⨯ Error: Maximum array nesting exceeded. Large nested arrays can be dangerous. Try adding intermediate objects.' A 0.62 MB JPEG (830k chars) lands, and so does a 3 MB 4032-px phone photo, because it is scaled to 2000 px and re-encoded to 305 KB. In Next 16.3.4's react-server-dom, bumpArrayCount adds a string argument's length to a 1e6 limit when the argument list has more than one item. uploadFile(leadId, parentId, name, image) passes the picture as a separate argument, so upload-picture.ts's PICTURE_CAP (8M) never applies. The UI now says Failed with Retry, and Retry fails the same way.
newIssues.fix: Pass one object: uploadFile({ leadId, parentId, name, image }) (strings under an object are not counted), or send a Blob or FormData. Until then, set PICTURE_CAP below 1,000,000 characters and keep redrawing smaller. Check other actions that take long strings as separate arguments (saveQuoteText html with pasted pictures, contract bodies with images) the same way.
